Title: Upstream re-ask backoff
Description: An adaptive charter with nobody answering re-asks the same unanswered plan request every tick forever (the v0.10.0 SS human WD-10 measurement: 601 of 635 events were this ticker noise). Back off the re-ask interval after K unanswered expiries, or hold one request open rather than expire-and-reopen. Deliberately DEFERRED OUT of v0.11.0 (ADR-0067 SS Deferred): it changes GOVERNED LIFECYCLE BEHAVIOR (the plan-request open/expire cycle itself), which under structural rule #2 mints a new WD-N plus its own ADR + gate - out of scope for a release whose defining posture is zero new capability. v0.11.0 governs only the DISPLAY of this volume (the audit read surface + the governed-actions@1 preset), not its cause.

Title: Generalized session revocation
Description: Make desktop logout real for every operator session, not only the paired-session tier v0.12.0 ships (SEC-34). Deliberately kept out of v0.12: it would change the auth posture of every existing session in the release immediately before the E-06 API freeze. Trigger: the E-06 security-audit capstone, or the multi-operator work (E-14/G14). Named explicitly in the v0.12.0 release criteria SS14 Deferred table.

Title: Resource-lifecycle audit
Description: CreateResource and UpdateResource (services/api/internal/server/server.go) chain no audit event at all; T-118c (v0.12.0) added one for DeleteResource only. A governance product whose core evidence claim is a chained audit trail should not have an unaudited resource lifecycle - every other governed mutation in the product (grants, workstreams, memories, context sources, pairing) chains an event.

Title: Audit provenance as a structured field
Description: AUD-34 (v0.12.0) attributes a paired-device approval by appending '#paired' to the resolvedBy actor string (services/api/internal/server pairingResolvedBy, consumed verbatim by services/policy-service/internal/store/store.go as the event Actor). audit-service's actor filter is exact-match, so filtering for operator:<id> misses that same operator's paired-device approvals (disclosed at T-114b review, a67b229). The structural fix is provenance carried as its own field on the event rather than encoded into the actor string - naturally sequenced with generalized session revocation (B-032) since both touch the same session/actor plumbing.

Title: Decide the fate of PUT /v1/resources/{id}
Description: The route is live, capability-gated, and correctly implemented (services/api/internal/server/server.go UpdateResource), but apps/web has never had a call site for it - verified at T-122b via a repo-wide search of apps/web/src. Keep it (design and build the update UI) or remove it (narrows CON-4's additive-only surface) must be decided at the E-06 API freeze, not carried past it silently - removing a live, unused route is easy before the freeze and a breaking change after it.

Title: Resource deletion blocked by session history
Description: sessions.resource_id (services/api/migrations/0002_sessions.up.sql) is a hard FK with no ON DELETE clause, so a resource that has EVER had a session opened against it - even one long since closed - can never pass DeleteResource's referential guard (T-118c, v0.12.0). Needs a migration decision: ON DELETE SET NULL on the FK, a soft-delete column on resources, or an explicit archival path.

Title: Design pass - font-weight and link-styled outlier
Description: Two inconsistencies surfaced during the Button migration (T-116/T-117, v0.12.0): a font-weight inconsistency across routes, and a text-primary link-styled control that does not match the ghost-Button idiom used everywhere else. The 14 documented className overrides T-117 recorded are the map for this pass. Also the natural home for E-05b (ConfirmDialog, B-018) if a future need argues past its v0.12.0 cut.

Title: Enforcement-of-enforcement test gaps
Description: Three silent-failure-of-a-guardrail modes surfaced in v0.12.0, none caught by an automated gate until directly probed: (1) an ESLint override block (the SEC-7 fetch exception) that matched no real file under either invocation path, dead since it was written (e0ac631); (2) Tailwind v4's content/@source scan silently excluded packages/ui/src until T-116 forced the question; (3) a workspace-package whole-module mock in a test can hide a real integration break. Each override/config-root/mock should carry a test asserting it actually matches/covers/exercises real code, not merely that it exists in a config file.

Title: General resource-management UI
Description: POST /v1/resources had no call site in apps/web until T-118b's demo-target action (v0.12.0) gave it one; there is still no general operator-facing form to register an arbitrary resource - today, creating one outside the demo path requires calling the API directly.
